item.title: Special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum on Online Safety to be held at 7pm Friday September 4th
item.description: A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th. The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?
item.content:encoded:
A special fijivillage Straight Talk Public Forum with Vijay Narayan will go live at 7pm Friday September 4th.

The theme of the forum is Online Safety: Connected and Protected?

The panelists for the public forum will be Online Safety Commissioner, Filipe Batiwale, Fiji Law Reform Commissioners David Solvalu and Valerie Narain.

The Straight Talk forum will focus on Online Safety Issues in Fiji, what is being faced by the Online Safety Commission, the feedback from the members of the public during the consultation process on the review of the Online Safety Act 2018, the call for age restrictions for Social Media, the response from victims, the changes being proposed and the reasons behind them amongst other issues.

You can also be part of the live audience by applying for registration with a question that you would like to ask during the forum.

The application to register details can be found on our website and facebook page, fijivillage.

You will receive a confirmation if you have been selected to be part of the live audience.

Please apply early to avoid any disappointment.

The show will be broadcast live at 7pm Friday September 4th on our Facebook, YouTube and X.

item.title: Damodar Group, Y3 Kofera Trust sign MOU for proposed 130-acre Nadi development
item.description: The Memorandum of Understanding establishes a framework for both parties to work together and begin the necessary due diligence before deciding on the final development concept and structure of the joint venture. The proposed development will be planned according to market demand and the long-term growth needs of the Denarau-Wailoaloa tourism and commercial belt and the greater Nadi area.
item.content:encoded:
The Memorandum of Understanding establishes a framework for both parties to work together and begin the necessary due diligence before deciding on the final development concept and structure of the joint venture.

The proposed development will be planned according to market demand and the long-term growth needs of the Denarau-Wailoaloa tourism and commercial belt and the greater Nadi area.

The Y3 Kofera Trust, which has historically been referred to as the Y3 Gopher Trust, is based in Narewa Village and serves as the corporate and investment arm of the Yavusa e Tolu, comprising Yavusa Navatulevu, Yavusa Sila and Yavusa Yakuilau.

The Trust holds customary rights over high-value tourism and commercial land in the Nadi delta, including Denarau Island, and has been involved in facilitating major resort developments on traditional land.

Damodar Group CEO Div Damodar says they look forward to combining the landowners' long-term vision for the land with the Group's experience in property development, investment and commercial precincts.

Damodar says their objective through the proposed Kofera Damodar Joint Venture is to build a sustainable real estate investment that supports the tourism sector and delivers lasting value to the community, local businesses and the wider Fijian economy.

The partnership is also expected to generate long-term economic returns, employment opportunities and direct welfare and educational support for the indigenous landowners.

Y3 Kofera Trustee and Board Secretary Samuela Tuidraki says the proposed partnership provides an opportunity for the landowners to participate directly in the long-term development and commercial use of their land.

Tuidraki says the Trust is committed to transforming the approximately 130 acres of native land into sustainable commercial ventures.

He says partnering with the Damodar Group would allow beneficiaries from Yavusa Navatulevu, Yavusa Sila and Yavusa Yakuilau to secure long-term economic growth and community benefits for present and future generations.

Initial due diligence assessments will begin immediately, with project planning, environmental assessments and master-design phases expected to follow.

Subject to satisfactory due diligence and agreement on the final joint-venture structure, Damodar Group and the Y3 Kofera Trust will work with relevant government agencies, local authorities, professional consultants and other stakeholders to prepare a development master plan for the site.

The parties say further announcements will be made as the due-diligence process progresses and the proposed development concept is refined.

item.title: PS for Employment warns Fijians after 300+ pay $100 each in alleged job scam
item.description: More than 300 people say they paid $100 each after being promised overseas employment opportunities, with more than 50 reportedly turning up at Nadi International Airport on Saturday expecting to leave Fiji, only to be told there was no flight booking for them. An affected individual, who spoke to fijivillage News on condition of anonymity, says they were told from February that a woman reportedly
item.content:encoded:
More than 300 people say they paid $100 each after being promised overseas employment opportunities, with more than 50 reportedly turning up at Nadi International Airport on Saturday expecting to leave Fiji, only to be told there was no flight booking for them.

An affected individual, who spoke to fijivillage News on condition of anonymity, says they were told from February that a woman reportedly based in New Zealand would assist them in travelling overseas for employment, including fruit-picking jobs.

He alleges each person was asked to pay $100 through M-PAiSA.

The individual says more than 300 people were involved in 32 groups, with about 10 people in each group.

He says people from Lomaiviti, Kadavu, Naitasiri, Namosi, Nadroga, Tavua, Rakiraki and Ba were among those involved.

The individual says payments started in February and they were initially told the first group would travel in March .

He says this was later changed to May and, as the months passed, they were eventually informed that the first group would depart last Saturday.

The man says he was told he would be employed on a sweet potato farm in Queensland, while two of his friends were told they would pick oranges in Melbourne and another was told he would work as a butcher in Sydney.

He says the organiser had been providing updates through a facebook group chat, but claims communication became less frequent as time passed.

The individual says more than 50 people from the first group travelled to Nadi International Airport on Saturday expecting to leave the country.

He says two people had travelled from Kadavu and another from Lomaiviti to Nadi expecting to board the flight.

The man says families had also travelled to the airport to farewell their relatives, believing they were leaving Fiji for the promised employment.

He says after waiting for hours for information about their flight, one of the affected people approached airport security and explained the situation.

The individual claims checks were then made and they were informed that there was no flight booking for the group that day.

He says some people had been waiting for the opportunity since February and claims some had even resigned from their jobs in anticipation of travelling overseas.

When contacted by fijivillage News today, Permanent Secretary for Employment Maritino Nemani says the Ministry became aware of the alleged recruitment issue this morning and is urging people who are being charged fees for recruitment outside Government programmes to report the matter to Police.

Nemani says the Government does not charge workers recruitment fees to participate in its Government-to-Government labour mobility programmes with Australia and New Zealand.

Nemani says people should also verify with the Ministry whether those offering overseas employment opportunities are legitimate before making payments or committing themselves to an arrangement.

He says despite the Ministry issuing public notices and making radio announcements advising people that Government does not charge recruitment fees under the programmes, Fijians continue to be attracted to other recruitment offers.

Nemani says the Ministry feels for the Fijians who went to Nadi International Airport based on promises that they would be travelling overseas for work.

item.title: Supreme Court rules public hospitals cannot refuse urgent medical treatment if patients are unable to make upfront payment
item.description: Public hospitals cannot refuse urgent medical treatment to patients because they are unable to make an upfront payment or guarantee payment, following a landmark ruling by the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court made the ruling in favour of Rajesh Chandra, administrator of the estate of his late son, who had taken legal action against the Permanent Secretary for Health, the Ministry of Health and the
item.content:encoded:
Public hospitals cannot refuse urgent medical treatment to patients because they are unable to make an upfront payment or guarantee payment, following a landmark ruling by the Supreme Court.

The Supreme Court made the ruling in favour of Rajesh Chandra, administrator of the estate of his late son, who had taken legal action against the Permanent Secretary for Health, the Ministry of Health and the Attorney-General.

Chandra's son who was 33-years-old suffered from moderate chronic kidney disease stage 3 and was admitted to Lautoka Hospital in June 2011.

The medical evidence at trial was that the 33-year-old man's condition had deteriorated to the point that he would need life-time dialysis treatment, although short-term dialysis treatment could prolong his life sufficiently to enable him to go to India for further testing and treatment that was available locally at the CWM Hospital and that the man was denied access to treatment because neither him nor his family could meet or guarantee to meet the costs involved.

In the judgement delivered, Justice Terence Arnold ruled that under the Public Hospitals and Dispensaries Act, patients admitted to public hospitals because they require urgent treatment or because of poverty cannot be required to pay upfront or provide a guarantee of payment before receiving treatment.

Justice Arnold found that Chandra's son required treatment and there was no legal basis for withholding short-term dialysis because he could not afford to pay for it.

He also found that the failure to provide the necessary treatment was not only a breach of the Public Hospitals and Dispensaries Act but also a failure by the medical staff involved to meet their common law duty of care.

Chandra was represented by Niven Padarath from Samual Ram Lawyers.

The case has been sent back to High Court for damages to be assessed.

item.title: Fijians consume twice the recommended daily salt intake- Chand
item.description: Fijians are consuming about 10 grams of salt every day, twice the World Health Organization's (WHO) recommended daily intake of 5 grams, raising concerns about the impact of high sodium consumption on cardiovascular health. This was highlighted by the Consumer Council of Fiji's Project Officer Nishalni Chand during her oral presentation at the Pacific Islands Health Research Symposium at the Fiji
item.content:encoded:
Fijians are consuming about 10 grams of salt every day, twice the World Health Organization's (WHO) recommended daily intake of 5 grams, raising concerns about the impact of high sodium consumption on cardiovascular health.

This was highlighted by the Consumer Council of Fiji's Project Officer Nishalni Chand during her oral presentation at the Pacific Islands Health Research Symposium at the Fiji National University in Nasinu.

Chand says according to the 2025 Fiji National STEPS Report, excessive sodium and low potassium intake are identified as two dietary risk factors that need greater attention in Fiji.

She says while Fiji's salt iodisation programme has been successful in addressing iodine deficiency, it does not address the amount of sodium people consume.

Chand says they are now looking at the potential introduction of potassium-enriched salt, where some of the sodium chloride in regular salt is replaced with potassium chloride.

However, she says access and affordability remain a significant challenge in Fiji because regular salt is supplied by at least nine importers and is available at a cheaper price, while potassium-enriched salt has only one supplier and is sold at a higher price.

She adds that existing provisions under the Food Safety Act could provide a pathway for introducing appropriate food standards and mandatory labelling without requiring new legislation.
